en: Run the portfolio and start every project with a charter and a clear go
Score proposals, sign charters and pass the gates before every start
every proposal is scored 1 to 5 on six weighted criteria, ranked and checked against your cut-off, so the monthly portfolio meeting starts from a ranked list
Business case with value and payback
investment, yearly benefit, years and discount rate give the net present value, the payback in months and a verdict against your payback limit
every project has a charter with purpose, objective and success measure, and a charter that waits too long for its sponsor shows as overdue to sign
Stage gate checks before a start
charter, scope, budget, team, risks and plan are six gates per project, each with a reviewer, evidence and a due date that warns before it is missed
RACI check for exactly one accountable
each activity is checked for one person responsible and exactly one accountable, and projects with rows to fix are flagged in the register
influence and interest give the engagement quadrant, and a sceptic with high influence is marked to win over first
Go and no-go decision log with review dates
every decision for a proposal or project keeps its readiness, conditions and review date, and a conditional go that is not reviewed on time turns overdue
amounts requested and approved, partly approved and declined requests and missing budget codes are separated so the finance partner knows what to open
the project days your team can give in a quarter are set against committed days and the effort of the proposals you would approve
each project is rated 1 to 5 against the six strategic objectives, so an objective that no project serves shows up at once
Project price from effort and margin
days by role at your own cost rates, vendors, contingency and margin give the cost, the price and how it compares with your charge rates
Quarterly budget with planned against actual
planned and actual spend of every project each quarter are compared with your amber and red limits

Portfolio register: every project the firm runs
One row for each project with client, sponsor, manager, dates, budget, status, stage, priority, health and progress; days late, budget share, schedule state, scope items and RACI checks fill in.
Project proposals waiting for a decision
One row for each candidate project with client, requester, estimated budget, effort and wished start; weighted score, rank, days waiting, net present value and a waiting state fill in.
Six criteria that every proposal is scored on, 1 to 5, with the weight of each; the weights should add up to 100 percent.
One row for each proposal with a score of 1 to 5 on each criterion; the weighted score, rank, budget and a cut-off check fill in.
Business cases: value, payback and return
One row for each proposal with the investment, the benefit per year, the years and the discount rate; net present value, payback in months, return and a verdict fill in.
Project charters: purpose, objective and signature
One row for each project with purpose, objective, success measure, version and the dates drafted and signed; sponsor, manager, budget, days open and a signature state fill in.
Objectives and success measures of every project
One row for each measure with baseline, target, current value, unit, dates and owner; progress to the target, time used and a state fill in.
Scope register: what is in and what is out
One row for each scope item with the reason, the owner, the date it must be agreed and the date it was agreed; days to agree and a state fill in.
Stakeholder register with influence and interest
One row for each stakeholder with influence and interest from 1 to 5 and their attitude; the engagement quadrant, the action and a priority number fill in.
RACI matrix: who does what in each project
One row for each activity with who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed; the number of accountable people and a check for exactly one fill in.
Stage gates: six checks before a project starts
One row for each gate item of a project with due date, reviewer, status, evidence and the date it passed; a state, the sponsor and manager phones fill in.
Go and no-go decisions for proposals and projects
One row for each decision for a proposal or project with date, decision, readiness, conditions and review date; the weighted score, a review state and the phone to call fill in.
Funding approvals: amounts asked for and approved
One row for each funding request with the purpose, amount requested and approved, approver, budget code and dates; the state, the amount not approved and the days waited fill in.
One row for each role a project needs with days, start date, who asked and who filled it; a state, days open and the phones to call fill in.
Phone of a person in the role
Assumptions, constraints and dependencies at start
One row for each assumption, constraint or dependency with its owner and the date it must be checked; days to check and a state fill in.
One row for each project with its contribution, 1 to 5, to each strategic objective; the total, the average and an alignment check fill in.
Quarterly portfolio budget: planned and actual spend
One row for each project and quarter with the planned and the actual spend; the difference, the share over plan and a state against your amber and red limits fill in.
Portfolio review log: one decision per project each month
One row for each project and monthly review with the decision, the health, the progress and the reason; the manager, days since the review and progress now fill in.
Clients with tier, industry and payment terms
One row for each client with contact, country, industry, tier and payment terms; the projects and budget you run for them and the proposals waiting fill in.
Team: roles, rates and weekly hours
One row for each team member with role, cost and charge rate per hour, weekly hours and the project hours target; projects managed, margin per hour and project days per quarter fill in.
Average days late of late projects
Average days from proposal to decision

Type a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion; the weights come from Scoring Criteria, then see the weighted score, the points above or below your cut-off, the rank among scored proposals and a verdict.
Points above or below the cut-off
Project price from effort, vendors, contingency and margin
Type the days for each role, the vendor costs, the contingency and the margin; cost per day comes from your Team sheet, then see the cost, the price and how it compares with your charge rates.
Margin you want on the price
Price against the value at charge rates
Contingency reserve from the risk level
Type the budget, the risk score and how much of the scope is still unclear; see the risk level, the reserve share and amount, and what the same share would mean across your whole portfolio.
Share of the scope still unclear
Extra reserve if the whole scope is unclear
Reserve if every project used this share
Three-point estimate: expected value and range
Type the best case, the most likely case and the worst case in days and your cost per day; see the expected days, the range, the days to promise at about 90 percent confidence and the cost.
Low end of the likely range
High end of the likely range
Days to promise at about 90% confidence

Team size and duration: the cost of adding people
Type the work in person-days, the team now, the people you add and the time lost on each channel; see how channels grow, how long the work takes and the team size with the shortest time.
Days gained or lost by adding people
Team size with the shortest time
Scope change impact on budget and end date
Type the effort of a change, the people on it, your cost per day, the budget, the reserve left and the baseline end; see the cost, the new end date, the new budget and the price to charge the client.
Price of the change to the client
Go/no-go readiness score from the gate answers
Score each of the six gate items from 0 (not started) to 5 (done and signed); see the readiness, the lowest item, how many items are fully ready and the decision it points to.
Cost of delay for a late start
Type the benefit per month, the weeks of delay, the planned start and what the waiting team costs; see the benefit lost, the idle cost, the total cost of delay and the new start date.
Share of the team that waits idle
Delay as a share of the project length
Break-even month when benefits repay the investment
Type the investment, the months before benefits start, the benefit and the running cost per month; see the break-even month and date and your net position after 12, 24 and 36 months.
Benefit per month needed to break even in 24 months
Portfolio capacity check: demand days against available days
Type the time lost to leave, the days already committed, the share of waiting proposals you approve and the quarters they spread over; the days available come from your Team sheet.
Time lost to leave and holidays

Type the people in the group, the people you add and the minutes each channel needs each month; see the channels to keep up, the hours they take and the size of your own stakeholder register.
Funding split by quarter from the phase shares
Type the budget, the share of each phase and the months each phase lasts; see how much money each of the first four quarters needs and what the quarterly budget of your portfolio plans next quarter.

Type the price, the cost to deliver, your win rate, the cost of preparing a bid and the bids per year; see the expected value of a bid and the win rate you need, then test other prices and win rates.

Hello {sponsor}, the charter of {project} is ready for your signature. {manager} drafted it {days_open} days ago. It holds the purpose, the objective and the budget of {budget}. Please read it and sign it this week.
Hello, we hold the go/no-go review for {subject} on {review_on}. The last decision was {decision}, with the conditions: {conditions}. Please come ready to confirm or change it.
Hello, the funding request for {project} ({purpose}) of {requested} has waited for your approval since {requested_on}. Please approve it or tell us what you need to change.
Hello, before you sign the scope of {project} we need your answer on one item: {item}. Reason given: {reason}. Please tell us by {agree_by} whether it is in or out of scope.
Hello {sponsor}, the kick-off of {name} is planned for {start}. {manager} will send the agenda. Please keep two hours free and tell us who else from your side should join.
Sponsor: gate review has open items
Hello, the gate review of {project} found an open item: {item}, status {status}, due {due}. Please help us close it before the next review.
Hello {requested_by}, we received your proposal {name} on {received} and scored it at {score} out of 5. We will send you our decision soon.

Hello {requested_by}, thank you for the proposal {name}. We cannot start it this quarter, so we move it to next quarter. We will come back to you with a date. Please tell us if your wished start of {wished_start} changes.
Client: we cannot take it now
Hello {requested_by}, thank you for the proposal {name}. After scoring it, we cannot take it on now. We would like to keep in touch and look at it again when our team has more room.
Hello {requested_by}, good news: {name} is approved. Your wished start was {wished_start}. We will send the charter and invite you to a scope workshop. Please name your sponsor.
Hello {contact}, we invite you to a scope workshop for {name}. We will agree what is in and what is out of scope. {manager} will send the date. Please bring the people who know your processes.
Hello {contact}, the contract for {name} is ready to sign. The start date is {start} and the planned end is {end}. Please tell us who signs for {client}.
Project manager: you manage the project
Hello {manager}, you are named project manager of {name} for {client}. The budget is {budget} and the start is {start}. Please prepare the charter draft and the first stakeholder list.
Hello {manager}, the charter draft of {name} is due two weeks before the start on {start}. Please send it to the sponsor {sponsor} and to the PMO lead for review.
Hello, the {item} gate review of {project} is on {due} with {reviewer}. Please bring the evidence: {evidence}. Status now: {status}.
Hello {prepared_by}, the business case for {proposal} has missing figures: benefit per year {benefit_year} and years {years}. Please complete it before the scoring session.
Hello {manager}, the charter of {project} is still unsigned after {days_open} days. Please call {sponsor} and agree a date. We do not start work without a signature.
Hello, agenda line for the portfolio review: {project}, managed by {manager}. Last decision: {decision}. Health: {health}. Progress at the review: {pct_done}. Reason: {reason}.
PMO lead: proposals waiting too long
Hello, the proposal {name} from {client} has waited {days} days for a decision. Its score is {score} and its rank is {rank}. Please put it on the next portfolio review.
Hello {filled_by}, you are staffed on {project} from {from_date} as {role} for {days_needed} days. {requested_by} will brief you. Please tell us about any clash with your other work.
Team member: request open for your role
Hello, we have an open request for a {role} on {project} from {from_date}, {days_needed} days. Can you take it? Please answer today so that we can plan the team.
Hello, please open a budget code for {project}. The funding is {purpose}, {requested} requested and {approved} approved. The request is {state}.
Hello, funding of {approved} is approved for {project} ({purpose}), under the code {budget_code}. Please open the budget and tell the project manager when it is ready.
Hello {name}, I would like a 30-minute talk about the project {project}. I want to hear your expectations, your worries and how you prefer to be kept informed. Which day this week suits you?
Hello {name}, please confirm your role on {project} in the RACI matrix. You are listed as {kind}. Tell us if you should be responsible, consulted or only informed for any activity.
Hello, portfolio summary for {project}: decision {decision}, health {health}, progress {pct_done}, now {now}. Reason: {reason}. Decisions needed from you are marked in the review log.

Hello, the proposal {name} from {client} is ranked {rank} with a score of {score} and an estimated budget of {est_budget}. The net present value is {npv}. We ask for your decision at the next portfolio review.
Hello, we need a {role} for {days_needed} days from {from_date} on {project}. Do you have someone free, and at what daily rate? Please answer within two working days.
Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.
Purpose: {col:charters.purpose}. Objective: {col:charters.objective}. We will know the project has succeeded when this holds: {col:charters.success}.
The approved budget is {col:charters.budget}. The project starts on {col:charters.start} and its baseline end is {col:charters.end}.

The charter was drafted on {col:charters.drafted_on}. Its state is: {col:charters.state}. Signing it gives the project manager the authority to use the budget and to ask the team and the client for time and decisions.
Any change of purpose, budget or end date goes through the change process and is signed by the sponsor.
The investment is {col:cases.investment}. The expected benefit is {col:cases.benefit_year} each year for {col:cases.years} years, discounted at {col:cases.rate}.
The net present value is {col:cases.npv}. The investment is paid back in {col:cases.payback_m} months and the return over the period is {col:cases.roi}. The verdict is: {col:cases.state}.
We accept a payback of up to {set:payback_max} months. A proposal with a negative net present value or a slow payback needs a strategic reason before it is approved.

The scope register holds {col:projects.in_n} items in scope and {col:projects.out_n} items out of scope. The first item in scope is: {col:projects.first_in}. The first item out of scope is: {col:projects.first_out}.

Everything that is not listed as in scope is out of scope. A request for anything outside the agreed scope goes through the change process, with its effect on budget and end date written down before it is approved.
The project runs from {col:projects.start} to {col:projects.end} with a budget of {col:projects.budget}.
The readiness at the decision was {col:golog.readiness}. Conditions: {col:golog.conditions}.
The decision is reviewed on {col:golog.review_on}. The review state is: {col:golog.state}.
A go with conditions is valid only while every condition is met. If a condition is missed, the decision returns to the portfolio review.
